info.title: Unipile LinkedIn API
info.description: LinkedIn data and messaging through your connected accounts: profiles, companies, chats, posts, network, structured search, and Recruiter job-slot credits. Bring your own LinkedIn account (connect once through the hosted authorization link), then read and act through one AIsa credential.

tags.name: Search
tags.description: Structured LinkedIn search and its parameter helper.

post.description: Returns a HostedAuthUrl that you send the end user to. They complete the LinkedIn sign-in on Unipile's hosted page, so no credentials ever touch your system. **Managed mode (recommended): omit `notify_url`** and AISA handles everything — poll `GET /apis/v1/unipile/me/accounts` until the account appears (usually within seconds of the user finishing the wizard); no webhook infrastructure needed on your side. **Self-hosted mode: pass your own `notify_url`** and Unipile POSTs `{"status":"CREATION_SUCCESS","account_id":"…","name":"…"}` to it when the flow completes — store that account_id, it is the identifier every other endpoint requires, and with your own webhook there is no listing endpoint to re-discover it (managed-mode users read `me/accounts` instead). The `name` you set here is echoed back in self-hosted mode, so use it to map the account to your own user. Reply 200 within 30 seconds or the event is retried five times; consider verifying a shared-secret header on your endpoint. Links expire on Unipile's daily restart regardless of `expiresOn`, so generate a fresh link each time a user wants to connect. Note: re-authorizing the same LinkedIn account creates a new account_id; earlier bindings remain listed until disconnected. $0.000001 per request.

url.description: Hosted authorization URL to send the user to.

type.description: `create` connects a new account, `reconnect` re-authenticates an existing one.

providers.description: Provider list, for example `["LINKEDIN"]`. Only used with `type=create`.

api_url.description: The Unipile server URL of this AIsa binding, for example `https://api68.unipile.com:19823`. Use the value documented here; a generic Unipile URL will not match the binding.

expiresOn.description: ISO 8601 UTC expiry, for example `2026-12-31T23:59:59.999Z`. Required by upstream, even though links also die on Unipile's daily restart.

name.description: Label echoed back in events so you can match the account to your own user.

notify_url.description: Callback notified once the connection completes.

success_redirect_url.description: Browser redirect after a successful connection.

failure_redirect_url.description: Browser redirect after a failed connection.

reconnect_account.description: Account id to re-authenticate. Required when `type` is `reconnect`.

bypass_success_screen.description: Skip Unipile's hosted success screen before the browser follows `success_redirect_url`.

disabled_features.description: Provider features to disable on the connected account: `linkedin_recruiter`, `linkedin_sales_navigator`, or `linkedin_organizations_mailboxes`.

get.description: Read side of the managed hosted-auth flow: when you create hosted links without your own `notify_url`, this is where the resulting `account_id` surfaces. Poll after the user finishes the LinkedIn wizard — the account usually appears within seconds. Returns only the accounts connected by this API key's owner; there is deliberately no tenant-wide listing. `status` is one of `running` (operational), `disconnected` (re-authentication needed — send the user a new hosted link with `type=reconnect`), `errored` (service interruption, retried automatically), `paused` (subscription issue), `degraded`/`partial` (per-product states). A freshly connected account is immediately usable even before its first status sync.

account_id.description: Unipile account id — the identifier every other endpoint requires.

name.description: LinkedIn display name of the connected account.

status.description: Connection status; see the hosted-auth flow docs.

is_locked.description: Whether API access to the account is locked.

get.description: Returns the AccountOwnerProfile of the connected LinkedIn account: name, headline, premium status, organizations, and contact details. Requires `account_id` as a query parameter. $0.005 per request.

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description: Connected account id delivered to your `notify_url` webhook by Hosted Auth Link (`DA…`).

get.description: Fetch a UserProfile by Unipile internal id or public identifier (e.g. `acme-ceo`). Public identifiers resolve through the classic API only. Optional `linkedin_sections` returns detailed sections — heavy section use is throttled by LinkedIn. $0.01 per request.

parameters.name: identifier
parameters.description: Member internal id or public identifier.

get.description: Fetch a CompanyProfile (industry, headcount, description, locations, and more) by company identifier. The identifier is a path parameter and accepts a public identifier (`microsoft`), a numeric company id (`1035`), or a URN (`urn:li:fsd_company:1035`). $0.01 per request.

parameters.name: identifier
parameters.description: Company public identifier, numeric id, or URN.

get.description: Returns a ChatList with cursor pagination. Right after connecting an account, the first upstream sync may still be running — recent conversations can take a few minutes to appear. $0.005 per request.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Pagination cursor from a previous page.

get.description: Returns a MessageList for the given chat_id with cursor pagination. Message objects embed attachments, reactions, and read receipts inline. $0.005 per request.
Streams the binary content of a message attachment. Take `message_id` and `attachment_id` from the `attachments[]` array inside message objects returned by Chat Messages. $0.005 per request.

parameters.name: attachment_id
parameters.description: Attachment id from the message's attachments array.

post.description: Sends a text message into an existing chat. Write action: LinkedIn applies daily messaging limits of roughly 100-150 messages per account, and the recipient must already share a conversation with you. Use Start Chat to reach someone you have no conversation with yet. $0.02 per request.

account_id.description: Connected account id the message is sent from.

post.description: Creates a LinkedIn conversation with one or more members and sends the opening message in a single call. **LinkedIn rule: the recipient must already be a 1st-degree connection** — list your connections first with the Relations endpoint and use those provider ids. Messaging a non-connection returns 403 `subscription_required` on this endpoint (LinkedIn only allows new chats with relations, InMail aside), and the account's own profile is not a valid recipient either. **To reach someone who is not yet connected, use the Connection Request endpoint** — it is not subject to this restriction; message them after the invitation is accepted. Write action: same daily messaging limits as Send Message. Pass each recipient's provider id (`ACoAA…`), which you can resolve from a public identifier with the User Profile endpoint. If a call does time out, verify the actual outcome via List Chats and the sent-invitations list before retrying. $0.02 per request.

account_id.description: Connected account id the message is sent from.

attendees_ids.description: Provider ids (`ACoAA…`) of the recipients — must be 1st-degree connections of the account.

post.description: Adds an emoji reaction to an existing message. Write action: counts toward the account's engagement limits. $0.02 per request.

reaction.description: Native emoji to react with, for example a thumbs-up.

get.description: Returns a PostList for the given user with cursor pagination. $0.01 per request.
Fetch one post by its id (activity URN form). $0.005 per request.
Returns the comment thread of a post by post_id. $0.005 per request.

post.description: Publishes a post as the connected account. Write action, and the result is publicly visible on LinkedIn, so treat it as irreversible. The request must be `multipart/form-data`: a JSON body is rejected while upstream parses attachments. Add an image with `-F "attachments=@image.jpg"`, mention someone by putting `{{0}}` in the text and passing `mentions[0][profile_id]` / `mentions[0][name]`, or post on behalf of a company you administer by passing `as_organization` with the company id. $0.02 per request.

account_id.description: Connected account id the post is published from.

text.description: Post body. Use `{{0}}` placeholders to reference entries of the `mentions` array.

attachments.description: Files to attach, one `-F "attachments=@file"` per file. Either several images or a single file of another type; images are capped at 6012x6012 px.

external_link.description: URL rendered as a preview card. Must also appear in `text` or it is appended automatically.

as_organization.description: Company id to publish on behalf of. Your account must administer that company page.

post.description: Posts a comment on an existing post. Write action: the comment is publicly visible. `text` is capped at 1250 characters. $0.02 per request.

parameters.name: post_id
parameters.description: Post id to comment on (activity URN).

account_id.description: Connected account id the comment is posted from.

post.description: Adds a reaction (like) to an existing post. Write action: the reaction is publicly visible. Pass the post's `social_id` as `post_id` — take it from the Post Detail or User Posts response, because the id visible in a LinkedIn post URL does not always resolve. $0.02 per request.

post_id.description: `social_id` of the post to react to, not the id from its URL.

get.description: Returns a UserRelationsList with cursor pagination. A freshly connected account may show an empty list until the initial upstream sync completes. $0.005 per request.
Returns an InvitationList of InvitationSent entries with cursor pagination. $0.005 per request.
Returns an InvitationList of InvitationReceived entries with cursor pagination. $0.005 per request.

post.description: Invites a LinkedIn member to connect — **this is the endpoint for reaching people who are not yet connections**, and it is not subject to the subscription restriction that Start Chat hits for non-connections. After the invitation is accepted the member appears in Relations and Start Chat works normally. Identify the recipient by their provider id (`ACoAA…`); resolve it from a public identifier such as `satyanadella` with the User Profile endpoint first. All parameters go in the JSON body (including `account_id`). The returned `invitation_id` can be canceled with Cancel Invitation. Write action: LinkedIn allows roughly 80-100 invitations per day depending on account age and activity, and accounts with little connection history may be blocked from sending them at all. $0.02 per request.

invitation_id.description: Id of the sent invitation; pass to Cancel Invitation to withdraw it.

usage.description: Percentage of the provider limit consumed.

account_id.description: Connected account id the invitation is sent from. Must be in the body, not the query string.

provider_id.description: Provider id of the member to invite (`ACoAA…`).

text.description: Optional note attached to the invitation, at most 300 characters.

delete.description: Withdraws a connection invitation that is still pending, before the recipient accepts or ignores it. Write action: only invitations returned by Invitations Sent can be withdrawn; once the recipient has acted on it there is nothing left to cancel. Take `invitation_id` from that listing and pass your `account_id` as a query parameter. $0.02 per request.

parameters.name: invitation_id
parameters.description: Id of the pending invitation to withdraw, from Invitations Sent.

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description: Connected account id that sent the invitation.

get.description: Maps human keywords (locations, industries, …) to the filter ids that LinkedIn Search expects. This helper endpoint is free of charge.

post.description: Executes a LinkedIn search with structured filters (`api`, `category`, `keywords`, optional `parameters[]` ids from Search Parameters). Returns ranked results. People search via the classic API is verified in production. $0.02 per request.

parameters.description: Structured filter objects from Search Parameters.

get.description: Returns total / used / available job-slot credits for the LinkedIn Recruiter contract attached to a connected Recruiter account. Behind the scenes this proxies the upstream v2 endpoint `GET /v2/{account_id}/linkedin/recruiter/job-slots-credits`; on AIsa the account id rides in the request path. $0.005 per request.

total.description: Total job slots in the Recruiter contract.
